classification.rationale: Transcript of a U.S. House subcommittee hearing on UAPs, featuring opening statements from members of Congress and introduction of witnesses. Primary content is official government proceedings, with testimony and organizational references. No extraordinary claims requiring hold; custody is clear (public congressional hearing).

_raw_list: The lack of transparency regarding UAPs has fueled wild speculation and debate for decades, eroding public trust in institutions.
AARO's budget remains classified, prohibiting meaningful oversight from Congress.
The Biden Administration's handling of the Chinese spy balloon shows the government is not prepared for these situations.
The U.S. government spent $1.5 million in taxpayer dollars on missiles to shoot down the Chinese balloon and two subsequent UAPs, yet little clarity has been provided.
A poll found that 68% of Americans believe the government is hiding information about UAPs.
Another poll found that nearly half of Americans believe the federal government is doing a very bad or somewhat bad job of dealing with UFO sighting reports.
The government has done nothing to assure service members that they will not face retribution for reporting UAP encounters.
The committee was denied access to a classified briefing (SCIF) prior to the hearing.
Witnesses will testify that UAPs have posed a serious safety threat.
The 2017 New York Times report revealed research on UAPs by the Defense Intelligence Agency.
The Office of the Director of National Intelligence has published public reports documenting UAPs.
On June 9, 2022, NASA announced it is commissioning a study to examine UAPs.
The stigma around reporting UAP incidents prevents a complete picture of the situation.
AARO Director Sean Kirkpatrick testified before the Senate that his unit has found no evidence of extraterrestrial activity.
NASA has stated they do not have evidence of extraterrestrial life.
Whistleblowers have reported harassment, intimidation, or stigma.
The Senate is taking up an amendment to the defense authorization bill to create a commission with broad declassification authority.
AARO's initial analysis found 171 uncharacterized UAP reports that appear to have demonstrated unusual flight characteristics or performance capabilities.
Former DNI John Ratcliffe confirmed the U.S. government is aware of many more UAP sightings that have not been made public.
